summary: Srednekolymsk Airport serves the remote town of Srednekolymsk in the Sakha Republic (Yakutia), one of the most isolated settlements in far northeastern Russia. Located above the Arctic Circle along the Kolyma River, the airport functions as a critical lifeline for residents, connecting them to Yakutsk and other regional hubs across vast, sparsely populated tundra. The facility primarily handles regional and commuter flights, given the extreme remoteness and challenging weather conditions of the region.
faqs:
Q: What is the airport code for Srednekolymsk Airport?
A: The IATA code is SEK and the ICAO code is UESK.

Q: Where is Srednekolymsk Airport located?
A: It is located near the town of Srednekolymsk in the Sakha Republic (Yakutia), in far northeastern Russia, above the Arctic Circle.

Q: What kind of flights operate from Srednekolymsk?
A: The airport primarily handles regional and commuter flights, mostly connecting to Yakutsk and other settlements within the Sakha Republic.

Q: When is the best time to fly to Srednekolymsk?
A: Summer months (June through August) tend to offer more reliable flying conditions, as extreme winter cold and low visibility can cause delays or cancellations.
transport_tips: Getting to and from Srednekolymsk Airport typically requires arranging local transport in advance, as taxi services are limited in this remote settlement. The airport is a short distance from the town center, but road conditions can be challenging depending on the season. Travelers should coordinate ground transportation with their hotel or local contacts before arrival, especially during winter when temperatures can drop dramatically.
local_tip: Pack extreme cold-weather gear regardless of the season—temperatures can plunge unexpectedly, and even short walks between the terminal and vehicle demand insulated, layered clothing suited to sub-Arctic conditions.
